_meta.description: Structured design-critic heuristics for the Rift marketing site. The agent MUST walk every P0 and P1 rule after taking screenshots; P2 rules are polish. Inspired by Vercel Labs web-design-guidelines (100+ rules) adapted for a single-page accessibility product.

severities.P0: Ship blocker — fix before any deploy or baseline refresh
severities.P1: Quality — fix in the same session if practical
severities.P2: Polish — log and fix next session

rules.check: No headline, logo, or CTA is clipped by the viewport edge, sticky nav, or parent overflow at any tested viewport.
In-page anchor links (#download, #story, etc.) land with the section heading fully visible below the sticky nav — not hidden under it.
No horizontal scroll at any viewport 320px and wider.
Display-size headings (clamp ≥ 4rem) have enough line-height + padding that ascenders/descenders don't clip.
Sections using overflow:hidden do not clip absolutely-positioned children that are meant to be visible.
Gradient transitions between sections (::before/::after bleed) look intentional, not like rendering artefacts.
Each section has exactly one focal point (headline OR hero visual OR primary CTA) that the eye reaches first.
No more than 3 distinct visual weights per viewport (e.g. display / subhead / body).
Section h2/h3 are visually distinct from body text (≥ 1.5× font-size ratio for h2 vs body p).
Primary CTA stands out from secondary actions — different size, weight, or contrast treatment.
Card grids have equal visual weight per card — no orphan/runt row (e.g. 3+1 at a breakpoint).
Badge / label text (research-badge, section-kicker) is clearly subordinate to headings, not competing.
Sticky nav does not visually dominate the current section content — it is backdrop, not foreground.
Hero section: headline + subcopy are not cramped — combined vertical air (margin + padding + gap) is roughly ≥ 40% of viewport height on desktop.
Section vertical padding never below ~24px between distinct content blocks at default font scale.
Stacked text blocks (p + p, p + meta, heading + blurb) have at least 1× their line-height as vertical gap.
Footer/meta stacks (build info, links, legal) are not a single undifferentiated wall of small grey text — they have distinct vertical rhythm or grouping.
No section where text+UI fills > 85% of its visible bounding box with zero intentional air.
Spacing between interactive elements (buttons, links) is consistent — no random tight/loose gaps.
Nav link spacing is even — no visually unequal gaps between navigation items.
All body copy achieves ≥ 4.5:1 contrast ratio against its effective background in light and dark themes.
In high-contrast theme, primary text achieves ≥ 7:1 where feasible.
No primary reading text renders below 14px computed font-size at any viewport × font-scale combination.
Secondary/meta text (build string, version, disclaimers) on dark backgrounds uses ≥ 0.5 alpha white, not ≤ 0.4.
Text placed over images or gradients has an overlay, shadow, or guaranteed contrast treatment.
Body copy line length stays ~45–75 characters on desktop (≥ 900px viewport). Use max-width on prose containers.
Body copy line-height ≥ 1.4; heading line-height ≥ 1.1.
Monospace / code-style text (inline-code, version strings) has adequate background or padding to separate from surrounding prose.
All primary interactive elements (nav links, buttons, CTAs) have ≥ 44×44px tap/click area.
Footer links have ≥ 44px hit height (padding counts).
Range inputs (sliders) have visible thumb ≥ 44×44px or the track itself is tall enough to tap.
Adjacent interactive elements have enough spacing that a fat-finger tap won't hit the wrong target.
Hover-only states (tooltips, expanded cards) have a non-hover fallback on mobile.
Sticky nav is readable and not transparent on scroll — background has sufficient opacity + blur.
Nav links do not crowd or wrap at 1024px (iPad landscape). On mobile (≤ 768px), non-essential links are hidden.
Nav CTA (Download) is visually distinct from text links — different background, pill shape, or weight.
Logo + nav are vertically centered; logo is not visually misaligned with link baselines.
Accessibility panel (Aa disclosure) does not break nav layout when opened.
Dark-mode nav background is distinct from section backgrounds below — no 'floating header' illusion.
Webfont (Plus Jakarta Sans) loads before or with graceful fallback — no FOUT that shifts layout.
Heading sizes use a consistent scale (--text-lg, --text-xl, --text-2xl, --text-3xl) — not ad-hoc pixel values.
All text respects --font-scale CSS variable — no elements with hard-coded px that ignore user scaling.
Letter-spacing on display type is slightly negative (-0.02em to -0.05em); body uses default or slight positive.
Numbers in stats / metrics use tabular-nums or monospace so columns align.

No orphan words at the end of headlines at common viewports (fix with
or max-width).
All three themes (light, dark, high-contrast) render without broken colors — no white-on-white or black-on-black.
Accent color (--accent) is used in ≤ 3 roles across the page (badges, links, focus rings) — not everywhere.
Dark sections (passage, download) use --void consistently; transitions between light and dark sections use gradients or clean edges.
Interactive states (hover, active, focus) are visible in all three themes — not just light.
Theme toggle updates instantly — no flash of wrong theme on page load (localStorage is read synchronously).
prefers-reduced-motion media query disables all non-essential animations (reveal, hero letter, tagline).

Reveal animations don't make content unreachable — section headings and lead text should not be gated behind .reveal if the section would render as a large blank area without them. Scrolling to the section must never show an empty white/dark rectangle.
Animations are short (≤ 1s for transitions, ≤ 2s for reveals) — nothing feels sluggish or disorienting.
Scroll-triggered reveals use IntersectionObserver, not scroll event listeners — no jank.
Looping animations (waveform, typing demo) don't drain battery — use will-change sparingly and pause when off-screen.

Animated demos (typing, autofix) render correctly in their FINAL state — wait for the full animation to complete and verify no text overflow, missing words, or broken layout. Shared CSS class names between demos (e.g. .demo-wrong, .demo-correct) must not conflict via global rules leaking position/opacity/animation into unrelated sections.
All interactive elements are reachable by Tab key in logical order.
:focus-visible outline is visible in all themes — uses --accent with sufficient contrast.
Skip-to-content link exists or first Tab stop is the primary nav.
Details/summary (accessibility panel) can be opened/closed with Enter and Space.
Focus order within the accessibility panel follows visual order (font buttons → theme buttons).
Hero image / video poster loads and is visible — no broken image icon or empty space.
Decorative images use aria-hidden='true' or empty alt; meaningful images have descriptive alt text.
SVG icons in tech cards and arch diagrams have role='img' and accessible name where needed.
Images are appropriately sized — no 4000px bitmap served at 400px display width.
Poster/fallback image is visible if video doesn't autoplay (Safari, low-power mode).
Page is usable at 320px width (iPhone SE) — no content cut off or overlapping.
Page is usable at 2560px width (QHD) — content doesn't stretch wider than max-width constraints.
Comparison table scrolls horizontally on mobile without breaking the page-level scroll.
Tech quartet uses explicit breakpoints (4/2/1 columns) — not auto-fit that causes 3+1 orphan.
Demo section (rift-demo-window) scales to fit viewport — no content overflow on small screens.
Font scale controls (A−/A/A+) + theme buttons are reachable on mobile — Aa panel opens cleanly.
All range inputs (speed slider in demo) have associated labels (aria-label or aria-labelledby).
Buttons have type='button' to prevent accidental form submission.
Custom styled inputs (sliders, toggles) match the theme's color tokens, not browser defaults.
No render-blocking resources beyond the main CSS — fonts load async or with display:swap.
Pretext vendor files load without 404s — all chunks (bidi.js, analysis.js, measurement.js, line-break.js) present.
Largest Contentful Paint element is the hero heading or image, not a below-fold section.
No layout shifts from late-loading content (CLS near 0).
Heading hierarchy is logical — h1 → h2 → h3 without skipping levels.
Sections use <section> with aria-labelledby pointing to their heading id.
Landmark regions (nav, main, footer) are present and unique.
Live regions (aria-live on announcements, demo text) update correctly for screen readers.
Schema.org structured data (@type SoftwareApplication) is valid JSON-LD.
Above the fold answers 'what is this?' and 'why should I care?' within 3–5 seconds of visual scanning.
Each modular section is self-contained (one idea, one CTA or takeaway) — sections don't bleed into each other conceptually.
Trust signals (open source badge, GitHub link, build number) are visible but subordinate to the value proposition.
Download section feels like a destination, not an afterthought — adequate visual weight and breathing room.
Footer is clearly the end — no ambiguity about whether more content follows.
